correctness.rationale: PASS: For fixed nonempty forbidden scattered word P, subsequence monotonicity yields the lower bound max_i rho_P(W_i). Greedy matching decomposes each W_i into phases U_{i,j} containing no next desired letter P[j+1]; concat those phase pieces across all inputs and share the marked p_j letters to build S embedding each input and with greedy rank exactly T=max input rank. If T=|P| every common supersequence contains P, otherwise this witnesses feasibility. The left-to-right rightmost-embedding deletion test is equivalent to embeddability of every input in the retained prefix plus remaining suffix; any retained position is irreversibly essential, proving inclusion minimality in O(k N+|P|) time and O(N+|P|) space. The statement handles k=1, empty inputs, repeated symbols and nonempty forbidden P. Independent direct brute check exhaustively compared 3150 binary pairs of lengths <=3 against their phase amalgamation, rank, and independently reduced inclusion-minimal witnesses.
residual_risks: 3150 finite brute-force binary checks are bounded; the universal theorem requires the phase and essentiality proofs.

value.rationale: PASS: This supplies a closed-form minimum greedy forbidden-pattern rank, an exact feasibility criterion, and an explicit efficient construction for a natural constrained common-supersequence problem explicitly raised by a 2026 primary article. The strict difference between shortest and inclusion-minimal is demonstrated by the infinite 0^m1, 10^m, P=11 family. The single-pattern hypothesis is substantive, and arbitrary k is covered.
